title: Bruton Place IV
disclosure: Self-initiated concept study; illustrative visual; not completed client work.
studyFocus: A compact reception and work floor organized around a clear arrival axis, focused work settings, and shared project space.
programAssumptions: A reception point with an adjacent waiting zone
A mix of focused desks, an enclosed meeting room, and an open project table
A material palette that separates public and focused-work zones
designQuestions: How can the entry provide orientation without a conventional reception desk?
Where should acoustic transitions occur between shared and focused work?
Can one continuous cobalt element connect arrival, storage, and wayfinding?
proposedDirection: Use a long cobalt datum to guide arrival, then offset charcoal work zones with soft-white circulation bands and acoustic screens.

title: Ethereal Gallery
disclosure: Self-initiated concept study; illustrative visual; not completed client work.
studyFocus: A quiet retail gallery that tests flexible display planes, measured pauses, and a legible path through a changing product edit.
programAssumptions: A small welcome point and a sequence of flexible display zones
Movable plinths for changing product groupings
A consultation niche screened from the primary circulation path
designQuestions: How little visual infrastructure is needed to make each display feel deliberate?
Can circulation alternate between compression and release without becoming confusing?
How might light define zones when the display arrangement changes?
proposedDirection: Compose a soft-white field of slim plinths and translucent screens, punctuated by cobalt thresholds and a charcoal consultation niche.

title: Obsidian Lounge
disclosure: Self-initiated concept study; illustrative visual; not completed client work.
studyFocus: An intimate hospitality lounge testing low-light orientation, varied seating clusters, and a central service element.
programAssumptions: A central service bar visible from the entry
A mix of paired, group, and perimeter seating
Clear service paths that do not divide the guest zones
designQuestions: How can guests read circulation clearly in a deliberately low-light setting?
Which seating geometries support both privacy and social energy?
Can reflected cobalt light establish orientation without becoming decorative glare?
proposedDirection: Anchor the plan with a charcoal oval bar, arrange soft-white seating islands around it, and use restrained cobalt light lines to mark movement.

title: Vortex Showroom
disclosure: Self-initiated concept study; illustrative visual; not completed client work.
studyFocus: A product showroom organized as a paced demonstration loop with a strong arrival marker and adaptable perimeter bays.
programAssumptions: A visible orientation point immediately inside the entry
A central demonstration zone with standing room
Adaptable perimeter bays for products of different scales
designQuestions: How can a visitor understand the full sequence without following a rigid route?
Where should demonstration, comparison, and conversation overlap?
Can a radial ceiling cue organize the room without competing with products?
proposedDirection: Set a cobalt radial guide above a charcoal demonstration core, with soft-white product bays arranged as an open, reversible loop.

title: Canvas Studios
disclosure: Self-initiated concept study; illustrative visual; not completed client work.
studyFocus: A salon program that studies station rhythm, shared preparation zones, and a calm progression from arrival to service.
programAssumptions: A reception point with a compact waiting area
A repeated line of styling stations with shared preparation storage
A screened wash zone separated from the arrival view
designQuestions: What station rhythm supports clear movement without feeling repetitive?
How can shared storage remain accessible while keeping the floor visually calm?
Can lighting distinguish consultation, styling, and wash activities?
proposedDirection: Build a measured sequence of cobalt-framed mirrors along a charcoal service spine, with soft-white circulation and a screened wash zone.
